Little Patterns, round 4: the Nook frame

A proposal for the phone-first rebuild you asked for on 11 October: one focused screen per game, Nook as the character with feelings, a Shapes game, faster speech, and no way out of a play screen. Nothing has been built. The screens below are static design mockups photographed at the S24 Ultra's sizes, the iPad and desktop.

Reviewed twice by Opus 5.5 and twice by Fable 5.1. Waiting for your approval and five answers.

Before and after on the S24 (portrait)

Left: the live build you tested. Right: the same game in the proposal.

Every screen, phone portrait

Swipe the rail. The question is in Nook's bubble, the answers are always in the same place at the bottom, and Help or Next sit under the thumbs.

Landscape and tablet

915 by 356 px after Chrome's bar. Nook moves to a narrow column, the task takes the middle, Help and Next sit on the right.

1024 by 698 px, Safari on the iPad 5. Nook is larger beside the task.

Nook with feelings

Nook keeps the original picture and gains ten feelings and a wave, drawn in its own style. Each feeling has its own face and posture, so no two look alike. Outside the Feelings game Nook only ever shows calm, happy, excited, proud or surprised, and never reacts to a wrong answer, to leaving, or to being away. Jof signed off this sheet on 11 October.

What changes for Arthur

Every screen now does one thing: Nook asks one question, the apples, shapes or feelings sit in the middle, and the answers are always in the same place at the bottom, with nothing else on the screen to tap away to. Nook becomes a friend with feelings of its own. Arthur can ask Nook to show any feeling, see it in Nook's whole body, hear it named, and watch Nook settle back to calm, and the games end with Nook sharing the moment (“We did it!”) instead of handing out stars. With fewer things to press, the same buttons always in the same places, quicker speech, and the ways out locked behind a grown-up’s press-and-hold, there is less to pull him away and more reason to stay and play.
Claude Opus 5.5, review pass 2

Your eleven findings, answered

  • Phones
    One frame, phone first. Nothing scrolls at 360 or 412 px portrait, 740 or 915 px landscape, or on the iPad. A harness fails the build on any overflow or clipped label.You said: Nothing fitted the S24 in either orientation.
  • Clutter
    Play screens drop from about fifteen pieces of chrome to five: shelf button, level pill, Nook's bubble, the task, Help or Next. Titles, labels, status lines, tabs, Back, brand and footer are gone.You said: Far too much on screen in every game.
  • Spelling
    The three picture cards show from the start. Hiding them is a Grown-ups setting. Keys end in Delete and Enter.You said: Pick the word, then spell it; pictures on by default.
  • Numbers
    One picture: three apples, a plus, two more apples in a dashed outline, the sum underneath, three answers. Help counts across both groups in one count. Over ten uses two ten-frames and Help fills the ten first.You said: Add was visually confusing.
  • Patterns
    Same bead strings, same answers, the rest removed. Make-your-own moves into the level pill.You said: Excellent, but cluttered.
  • Feelings
    Nook has the feelings. Tap a card and Nook performs it full screen, says the word, settles back to calm, and returns to the board with a tick. No Back, no sound button. Done is there for sound off.You said: No context or structure; Back unused; Sound pressed constantly.
  • Speech
    The pauses are trimmed and the words joined in the voice build. Same recordings, no hurry. A listening page lets you pick the pace.You said: Far too slow on a completion line.
  • Icons
    Two round faces in Nook's colours (one calm, one sad), and a palette with four colours and a brush.You said: Feelings and Paint need icons.
  • Tapping out
    Nothing on a play screen leads out. The K-Pop BOOM door, settings and player switching sit behind a two-second press-and-hold on the shelf. The games can run full screen from the home screen, locked with Guided Access or Samsung App pinning.You said: Arthur gets out of the game or browser.
  • Shapes
    Tap each side to light and count it, then choose the number. Or name the shape from three words. Nook holds the shape up when it is right.You said: A new game played at school.
  • Nook
    Nook is now drawn as a character with ten feelings and a wave, and reacts to play with calm, happy, excited, proud or surprised, never to mistakes. Tapping Nook always gets a small, kind response.You said: Nook as the one with feelings.

The review loop

Opus 5.5, pass 134 numbered recommendations. Rejected outright: "diamond" as a shape, the four-colour feelings groups, faces on the answer cards, a sound toggle on play screens, the Grown-ups gate on every screen. Wrote the motion specification (durations, easing, what never moves).
Fable 5.1, pass 1Answered all 34 by number: 29 accepted, 2 accepted in part, 1 pushed back (whole-sentence clips, later), 3 deferred to you. Re-rigged Nook, moved the gate and the mute off play screens, re-shot at six sizes.
Opus 5.5, pass 2"The design is now right." Approved section 4 as the build brief with nine must-fix items (Feelings layouts at landscape and tablet, the Nook rig, the shelf mute, labels at 360 px, the Add row) and ten should-do items for the build.
Fable 5.1, pass 2All nine applied and re-shot; the harness now fails on clipped content and cut-off labels, not only page overflow. Final set is clean at all six sizes.

Full text: docs/little-patterns-review-round-4.md and the four pass files under docs/little-patterns-round-4/. Education paths checked: EYFS and Development Matters (number, shape, self-regulation), NCETM number structures, TEACCH visual structure, Attention Autism, AAC practice.

Five things only you can decide

  1. Lock the device
    Run the games full screen from the home screen and lock them: Guided Access on the iPad, App pinning or Samsung Kids on the S24. On the iPad, players are set up once more in the home-screen app.
    Recommended: yes.
  2. Feelings colours
    Does school use a colour scheme for feelings (for example the four zones)? If so, which one, so the cards match it exactly. Otherwise the cards stay one neutral colour.
    Recommended: neutral unless school uses one.
  3. Keyboard layout
    Is Arthur's Grid keyboard ABC or QWERTY? The letter keys will match it.
    Default until you answer: ABC.
  4. Nook's new drawing
    The vector Nook has a slightly larger face than the picture Arthur knows. The feelings sheet below is the sign-off.
    Recommended: approve the sheet.
  5. Help glyph
    Keep the hand sign you passed in round 3, or use the Mulberry help symbol?
    Recommended: keep the hand sign.

What happens on your approval

  1. Build the frame, the shelf, the gate and the manifest; move Count, Add, Words and Patterns into it; keep every saved level and position.
  2. Draw Nook into the games with the motion specification; build Feelings and Shapes.
  3. Render the 50 new voice lines (one to two days at the 100-a-day cap) and the trimmed, joined speech, with a listening page for you.
  4. Rewrite the UI tests for the new structure, add Shapes and Feelings tests and the six-size layout check.
  5. Deploy a preview on a kpopboom branch for the S24 and the iPad before anything goes live.

Nothing in the game folder has changed. The mockups live in docs/little-patterns-round-4/mockups/ and are not on the deploy list.
